office_does: The county clerk keeps Superior Court records and exhibits, collects court fees, fines and restitution, and serves as the court's administrative and financial office.
race_blurb: Clerk Melissa Beaton, a Democrat first elected in 2019 after two decades in Superior Court administration, faces independent Amanda Toscano, a real estate agent who qualified for the ballot with write-in votes in the primary. The race pairs long court experience with a first-time candidate who says she ran to give voters a choice.

candidates.summary: Incumbent clerk since 2019 and former Superior Court manager, also a Mount Vernon city councilmember, running on legal and court-administration expertise.
highlights: Says she modernized services and implemented e-filing while running a $3 million, 19-person office [S1]
Past president of the state county clerks' association; certified court manager [S1][S2]
Warned of budget-driven staff losses for 2027 [S4]
Endorsed by the Skagit County Democrats and officials of both parties [S3][S5]

experience.basis: Incumbent clerk since 2019 with about two decades of Superior Court administration before that; runs on that expertise.

candidates.summary: Real estate agent and first-time candidate who qualified as a write-in and runs on customer service and document-handling experience.
highlights: Says she will make court procedures 'clear, consistent, and customer friendly at the counter and online' [S1]
Pledges to be 'a careful steward of public resources, prioritizing needs over wants' [S1]
Said she entered the race to give voters a choice; of the court, she said 'Obviously, I've never been there' [S2]
Promoted on SkagitResidents.com as one of four 'constitutional' write-in candidates [S3][S4]

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no court experience who ran to give voters a choice against a long-serving incumbent.

spending.basis: Single pamphlet pledge to be 'a careful steward of public resources, prioritizing needs over wants'; no specific budget position.
